audit.scope: Next.js frontend + Supabase RLS migrations + market-data proxies + client-side E2E sync. Backend runtime (Supabase managed), Vercel/CI dashboards, live DB schema and runtime a11y/CWV NOT assessed.

stack.backend: Supabase (Auth + Postgres RLS + Realtime + Edge Function)

findings.title: encrypted_records upsert uses onConflict:"id" but committed migration declares composite PK (user_id, record_type, id)
findings.description: upsertEncryptedRecord() calls .upsert(payload, { onConflict: "id" }). Postgres requires a UNIQUE/PK constraint matching the ON CONFLICT target. supabase/migrations/0001_initial_sync.sql line 38 declares `primary key (user_id, record_type, id)` and no unique constraint on id alone. Any environment provisioned from the committed migrations therefore has no `id`-only constraint, and every sync write would fail with 42P10 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the ON CONFLICT specification'. Production works only because the live DB schema has drifted to a PK/unique on id alone (corroborated by project notes).
findings.impact: Disaster recovery, staging rebuilds, and new-region provisioning from the tracked migrations produce a database on which all encrypted-record writes fail. The repository is not a faithful source of truth for the production schema; DR is effectively broken.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the migration with production reality: add a migration that sets the real live constraint (unique/PK on encrypted_records.id) OR change upsert to onConflict:"user_id,record_type,id" to match the declared PK. Add a schema-diff check (supabase db diff) to CI so drift is caught. Decide the intended PK deliberately (id-alone vs composite) and make code+migration agree.
findings.verification: Provision a throwaway Supabase project from supabase/migrations only, run a sync write end-to-end; it must succeed. Add `supabase db diff` in CI returning empty against production.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy is Report-Only; no enforced CSP in production
findings.description: Middleware only sets `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`. next.config.ts sets HSTS, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy but no enforcing CSP. Report-Only blocks nothing; it provides zero runtime XSS mitigation. For a financial app rendering some HTML via dangerouslySetInnerHTML (landing/FAQ) this leaves React output escaping as the only XSS defense.
findings.impact: Any future/overlooked injection sink (third-party script compromise, a stored value reaching dangerouslySetInnerHTML) executes unmitigated. No defense-in-depth against script injection.
findings.recommendation: Complete the documented staged rollout: analyze collected reports, then switch to enforcing `Content-Security-Policy` with the same nonce+strict-dynamic policy. Verify Vercel Analytics/Speed Insights (same-origin /_vercel/*) and TelemetryDeck (connect-src nom.telemetrydeck.com already present) still function under enforcement.
findings.verification: After flip, load every route with devtools open: zero CSP violations for first-party functionality; an injected inline <script> is blocked.

findings.title: No crash/error reporting or backend error monitoring
findings.description: The only telemetry is product analytics (TelemetryDeck), web analytics (Vercel Analytics) and perf (Speed Insights). No Sentry/Bugsnag/Rollbar/OpenTelemetry present (grep of package.json/src/app is empty). Server routes log via console.warn/error only; there is no aggregation, alerting, correlation IDs, or a way to detect a spike in 5xx, failed decryptions, calc errors, or market-data provider outages.
findings.impact: Production incidents (bad calc, provider outage, auth failures, exceptions) are invisible until users report them. Phase 19 observability requirements unmet for a product handling financial data.
findings.recommendation: Add an error/crash reporting SDK (e.g. Sentry) for both client and server routes with PII scrubbing (never log payloads, tokens, emails). Add alerting on 5xx rate, market-data 502 rate, and CSP report volume. Add health/readiness checks to uptime monitoring.
findings.verification: Throw a test exception in a route and confirm it appears in the error tool with no PII; confirm an alert fires on synthetic 5xx burst.

findings.title: Form labels not programmatically associated with inputs
findings.description: In login-form.tsx and signup-form.tsx, <label style={labelStyle}>E-mail</label> is a sibling of the <input> with no htmlFor/id and no wrapping. The label is not exposed as the input's accessible name to assistive technology. Same pattern in signup-form.tsx (lines 133/134, 145/146, 158/159). Likely systemic across the inline-styled forms.
findings.impact: Screen-reader users are not told which field they are in; violates WCAG 1.3.1 (Info & Relationships) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). Affects the primary auth path.
findings.recommendation: Associate each label via htmlFor/id (or wrap input in label, or add aria-label). Sweep all forms (auth, transactions, instruments, settings, import) for the same pattern.
findings.verification: axe-core reports no label violations; VoiceOver/NVDA announces each field's label on focus.

findings.title: Vercel Analytics + Speed Insights load unconditionally with no consent gate
findings.description: <Analytics /> and <SpeedInsights /> are mounted in the root layout for every visitor including the public marketing site, before any consent interaction. The privacy policy (app/privacy-policy/page.tsx lines 92-94) DOES disclose both, and both are cookieless by default, but they process IP-derived data for EU visitors. The app intentionally shows no consent banner (justified only via 'necessary Supabase cookies'), which does not squarely address whether analytics needs consent or a documented legitimate-interest basis.
findings.impact: Potential ePrivacy/GDPR exposure for EU users if analytics is deemed non-essential and lacks a valid lawful basis. This is a legal determination, not a confirmed code defect.
findings.recommendation: Obtain DPO/legal sign-off on the lawful basis for Vercel Analytics/Speed Insights; document a legitimate-interest assessment, or gate them behind consent, or confirm they qualify as strictly-necessary/exempt. Keep policy and implementation in lockstep.
findings.verification: Legal/DPO written sign-off referencing the exact processors; network tab confirms no device storage is written pre-consent.

findings.title: Inflation/floating treasury bonds silently fall back to margin-only rate when macro data is missing
findings.description: bondPeriodRate() returns Math.max(0, marginOverBase) when CPI (line 137) or NBP reference rate (line 129) is unavailable for a coupon period. The hardcoded fallback CPI_YOY ends 2026-06 and NBP_REFERENCE_RATES ends 2026-03. Live values are normally injected by MarketReferenceRateBootstrap, but if that fetch fails, later coupon periods price at margin-only, understating value. A detector exists (position-valuator.ts treasuryBondMacroGaps / bondPeriodHasMacroData) but this audit did not confirm the UI actually surfaces the gap to the user on every affected view.
findings.impact: A bond's displayed value can be silently too low when macro data is stale/unavailable, misleading the user about portfolio value and return.
findings.recommendation: Confirm every surface that shows bond value also renders the treasuryBondMacroGaps warning (badge + 'wycena przybliżona' note) and never presents a margin-only fallback value as current. Add a test asserting the warning propagates to dashboard/positions/reports when a period lacks macro data.
findings.verification: Unit + component test: a bond whose period lacks CPI shows a visible 'approximate/stale' indicator on dashboard, positions and reports.

findings.title: Open-redirect guard bypassable in /auth/callback and /auth/confirm via backslash/control-char next param
findings.description: safeNext = next.startsWith('/') && !next.startsWith('//') ? next : '/dashboard'. Verified with Node's WHATWG URL parser: next='/\evil.com' and next='/\t//evil.com' pass the guard and new URL(safeNext, origin) resolves to https://evil.com/. Same guard in app/auth/confirm/route.ts line 23. Reachability is limited: the redirect only executes after a successful exchangeCodeForSession / verifyOtp (valid one-time token required), and the login form ignores `next` (redirects to hardcoded /dashboard).
findings.impact: Phishing-style redirect to an attacker origin after a legitimate auth callback, if an attacker can craft a callback URL carrying both a valid token and a malicious next. Low likelihood due to the one-time-token gate.
findings.recommendation: Harden the guard: reject any next containing backslashes or control characters; better, parse with new URL(next, origin) and require the resolved .origin === origin before redirecting. Also confirm the Supabase Auth 'Redirect URLs' allowlist is tightly scoped (dashboard config, not assessed here).
findings.verification: Unit test: next in ['/\\evil.com','/\t//evil.com','//evil.com','https://evil.com'] all resolve to a same-origin path; only same-origin relative paths are honored.

findings.title: Public rate limiter keys on spoofable leftmost X-Forwarded-For and is per-instance in-memory
findings.description: clientKey() uses the first entry of X-Forwarded-For, which on Vercel is client-supplied (the platform appends the real IP). An attacker can rotate a spoofed leftmost value to reset the per-IP counter, bypassing the limit. State is also in-memory (Map), so it is per-instance on Fluid Compute and resets on scale/redeploy (self-documented at lines 5-7).
findings.impact: The 60 req/min (and 5/30 for waitlist/csp) caps are evadable, allowing an unauthenticated client to burn upstream provider quota (Yahoo/NBP) and cache. Impact bounded because endpoints only proxy public data and hold no user state.
findings.recommendation: Key on the Vercel-provided client IP (x-real-ip or the rightmost trusted XFF hop / request.ip), not the leftmost XFF. For durable limits across instances, back the limiter with Upstash Redis/KV. Keep the honeypot + zod validation as layered controls.
findings.verification: Send requests with a rotating spoofed X-Forwarded-For; the limiter must still throttle by true client IP.

findings.title: Primary (app-shell) logout does not clear the pending-sync localStorage queue
findings.description: handleLogout() clears the IndexedDB decryption key (clearCachedUserDataKey) then signs out, but does NOT call clearPendingSyncOperations(). The settings-page logout (settings-page.tsx lines 463-466) does clear it. The pending queue key `investor-web-pending-sync-v1` is a single global localStorage key (not user-scoped). After a sidebar logout with a non-empty queue, user A's queued operation metadata (record id, record_type, timestamps, device_id) and encrypted payloads persist for the next browser user. Cross-account WRITE is blocked by RLS with-check (auth.uid()=user_id), so no data corruption; the residue is encrypted-payload + plaintext operation metadata only.
findings.impact: On a shared browser, user B can read localStorage metadata revealing that user A had pending changes of certain record types/counts/timing. No plaintext portfolio values leak. Also produces confusing sync errors for B.
findings.recommendation: Call clearPendingSyncOperations() in app-shell handleLogout() (parity with settings logout). Consider namespacing the queue key by user id and clearing on account switch.
findings.verification: Log in as A, create an offline/failed op (queue non-empty), log out via sidebar; localStorage has no investor-web-pending-sync-v1 entry.

findings.title: parseAmount replaces only the first comma and rejects/misreads thousands separators
findings.description: value.trim().replace(',', '.') replaces only the first comma. '1 234,56' -> '1 234.56' -> NaN -> null; '1.234,56' -> '1.234.56' -> null; '1,234' (pl thousands) -> '1.234' -> 1.234. Behavior is locale-consistent for pl-PL decimals and is intentionally parity-locked with the native app, but it can reject or misread grouped input a Polish user might type.
findings.impact: Users entering grouped amounts get rejected or (for '1,234') a value 1000x too small. Bounded by the pl-PL decimal convention and the shared native contract.
findings.recommendation: If the shared contract allows, strip spaces and known grouping separators before parsing, and reject ambiguous inputs explicitly with an inline hint (e.g. 'użyj przecinka jako separatora dziesiętnego'). Otherwise document the constraint in the field help.
findings.verification: Table test covering '1 234,56', '1.234,56', '1,234', '1234.56', '1234,56' with expected results and clear rejection.

findings.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML on landing/FAQ; JSON-LD not escaped for </script> breakout
findings.description: app/page.tsx injects LANDING_NAV_HTML/LANDING_BODY_HTML (build-time static constants in app/_landing/content.ts) and app/_landing/landing-hero.tsx injects an html prop; app/faq/page.tsx injects JSON.stringify(faqJsonLd) into a <script type=application/ld+json>. All sources are currently static/developer-controlled, so no live XSS. However JSON.stringify does not escape '<', so if faqJsonLd ever includes user/CMS text containing '</script>' it breaks out; and the landing HTML pattern is fragile if any dynamic value is ever interpolated.
findings.impact: No current exploit (static content). Latent XSS if any of these sinks later receives dynamic/user data.
findings.recommendation: Escape JSON-LD by replacing '<' with '\u003c' before injection. Add a lint rule / code comment forbidding dynamic input into the landing dangerouslySetInnerHTML constants. Re-evaluate once CSP is enforced.
findings.verification: Snapshot test that JSON-LD output contains no raw '<'; review confirms landing HTML remains static.

findings.title: App-lock PIN stored as a weak deterministic hash in sessionStorage
findings.description: hashPin() is a 'simple deterministic hash' (self-described as 'not a security boundary') persisted in sessionStorage. It is a convenience idle-lock over data already protected by the Supabase session and the AES-GCM decryption key; it does not gate the ciphertext or the key.
findings.impact: The PIN lock can be trivially bypassed/reversed by anyone with the tab open, but it protects nothing cryptographically. Risk is limited to giving a false sense of a stronger lock than it is.
findings.recommendation: Keep as a UI convenience but ensure product copy does not present it as securing data at rest. If a real local lock is desired, gate the in-memory decryption key behind PIN-derived unlock. Otherwise document intent.
findings.verification: Confirm marketing/settings copy does not claim the PIN protects stored data; optional: derive lock from a KDF.

findings.title: getSession() used once (client UI) — acceptable; not an authz boundary
findings.description: One getSession() call for client-side UI state. All server-side authorization (middleware.ts, app/(app)/layout.tsx, app/api/sync/bootstrap/route.ts) and the real data boundary (RLS) use getUser(), which revalidates the JWT with the auth server. The getSession() here is not used as a trust boundary.
findings.impact: None (no authz decision relies on the unvalidated session).
findings.recommendation: No change required; note for reviewers so it isn't 'fixed' incorrectly. Keep getUser() for any future server authz.
findings.verification: Confirm no server route or RLS-bypassing logic depends on getSession().

findings.title: XIRR uses Actual/365 (ignores leap years) — Excel-compatible convention
findings.description: MS_PER_YEAR = 365 days; computeXirr uses Newton-Raphson with a bisection fallback over [-0.9999, 10]. Day-count is Actual/365 fixed (leap years not weighted), matching Excel XIRR. Solver is robust and returns null for unsolvable/degenerate cashflows.
findings.impact: Sub-basis-point differences vs Actual/Actual over long horizons; consistent with the reference convention.
findings.recommendation: Document the day-count convention next to the function and in any user-facing methodology note. No code change needed.
findings.verification: Golden test vs Excel XIRR on a reference cashflow set (already partially covered by investor-snapshot tests).

findings.title: Market-data cache and rate-limit are in-memory per-instance
findings.description: Both cache.ts and rate-limit.ts use module-level Maps. On Vercel Fluid Compute these are per-instance and reset on redeploy/scale. Route handlers also set fetch next.revalidate, giving a second cache layer. Acceptable for a public-data proxy; documented.
findings.impact: Cache hit ratio and rate-limit accuracy vary with instance count; no correctness impact.
findings.recommendation: If provider quotas become a concern, move cache/limit to Upstash Redis/KV or rely on Vercel Data Cache tags. Otherwise leave as-is.
findings.verification: Load test observing provider call volume under scale; confirm within provider limits.

findings.title: formatCurrency renders whole units (maximumFractionDigits: 0)
findings.description: formatCurrency uses maximumFractionDigits: 0, hiding grosze in display. Underlying values retain precision (roundToGrosz in the bond math). Ensure any surface where sub-unit precision matters (exports, detailed reports, tax figures) uses a precise formatter.
findings.impact: Displayed rounding may confuse users comparing to a broker to the grosz; underlying math is unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Provide a precise formatter for detail/report/export contexts; keep the compact one for KPIs.
findings.verification: Review reports/exports to confirm precision where required.

findings.title: xlsx pulled from SheetJS CDN tarball; historical prototype-pollution CVEs; client-side self-parse only
findings.description: "xlsx": "https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/xlsx-0.20.3.tgz" — SheetJS's official distribution channel (they left npm), integrity pinned via package-lock. 0.20.3 postdates the known prototype-pollution/ReDoS advisories (CVE-2023-30533, CVE-2024-22363). Parsing is client-side on the user's own imported file, so blast radius is the user's own tab.
findings.impact: Low: user-parses-own-file; patched version. Supply-chain note: non-registry source means npm audit won't track it.
findings.recommendation: Track SheetJS advisories manually (out of npm audit scope), keep the version current, and validate lockfile integrity in CI. Consider read-excel-file (already a dependency) for the common paths if xlsx breadth isn't needed.
findings.verification: Confirm lockfile integrity hash is enforced (npm ci); watch SheetJS releases.

findings.title: Unused variable warning in beta-waitlist route
findings.description: eslint warns: '_removed' is assigned a value but never used (destructure-to-omit pattern). Cosmetic.
findings.recommendation: Prefix-ignore is already the convention; either add an eslint-disable-next-line or omit via a helper. Trivial.

findings.title: Verify preview deployments are noindex and isolated from production data/secrets
findings.description: robots.ts/sitemap.ts hardcode host zecca.pl and disallow private routes, but preview *.vercel.app indexing, and whether preview environments receive production Supabase/Airtable secrets, depends on Vercel project settings not available to this audit. Vercel adds X-Robots-Tag: noindex to previews by default, but this must be confirmed along with env-scoping.
findings.impact: If previews carry production secrets or are indexable, that is a data/SEO exposure (would be BLOCKER-class if confirmed).
findings.recommendation: Confirm in Vercel: previews use separate (non-production) Supabase project and Airtable base; preview protection enabled; X-Robots-Tag noindex present on preview responses.
findings.verification: curl a preview URL: X-Robots-Tag: noindex present; env vars for preview scope point to non-prod resources.
